mechanism: The listsinceblock handler (src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1968 define-rpc, :1996) parses its first argument with %wallet-parse-txid (:1749-1753), a helper whose error message hardcodes the field name "txid": (error 'bl.rpc:rpc-error :code +rpc-invalid-parameter+ :message "txid must be of length 64 (not including any '0x' prefix)"). Core calls ParseHashV(request.params[0], "blockhash") (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/transactions.cpp:595), and ParseHashV (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/util.cpp:117-125) formats the NAME it was given into the message. Two further divergences fall out of the same helper, both confirmed by execution: Core's d3056bc message is "%s must be of length %d (not %d, for '%s')" -- it reports the actual length and echoes the offending string -- and Core has a SECOND branch, "%s must be hexadecimal string (not '%s')", for a 64-character argument that is not hex. Our helper's single message text ("... (not including any '0x' prefix)") is Core's wording from before that change, and it answers the same string for a wrong-length argument and for a right-length non-hex one. The finding's quoted core_does string is therefore stale for d3056bc; the field-name mechanism it identifies is exactly right.
consequence: A caller who passes a malformed blockhash to listsinceblock is told the wrong parameter is at fault, with no length and no echo of the value. Nothing is mis-loaded and no value is acted on, so it is a string divergence: S3. It is directly asserted by Core's own suite -- wallet_listsinceblock.py:93 expects -8 "blockhash must be of length 64 (not 11, for 'invalid-hex')" and :95 expects -8 "blockhash must be hexadecimal string (not 'Z000...')" -- so both assertions fail against us today, the second one because the non-hex branch does not exist at all.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-wallet-s3, warm container; probe build/ga11probe/p1.lisp (bitcoin-lisp.tests::ga11-p1) on a regtest wallet, every call through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method with bl.rpc::%normalize-rpc-params. Results: listsinceblock "00" -> (:RPC -8 "txid must be of length 64 (not including any '0x' prefix)"); listsinceblock "zz" -> the same; listsinceblock with 64 'z' characters -> the same message again (Core would say "blockhash must be hexadecimal string"). Control that the parse is the only thing diverging: listsinceblock with 64 'a' characters -> (:RPC -5 "Block not found"), which is Core's RPC_INVALID_ADDRESS_OR_KEY "Block not found" from transactions.cpp:598. Control that the helper is shared: gettransaction "00" -> the identical message, and there the field name "txid" is correct (though the tail still diverges -- wallet_basic.py:172 expects "txid must be of length 64 (not 34, for '000...')"). Our tree has exactly two sites with this string: src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1752 and src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2925. Core at d3056bc: rpc/util.cpp:117-125, wallet/rpc/transactions.cpp:595, test/functional/wallet_listsinceblock.py:93,95.
fix_shape: Port ParseHashV rather than patching the one call site: give the wallet a %wallet-parse-hash (value name) that takes the field name as an argument and reproduces both of Core's branches -- "<name> must be of length 64 (not <actual>, for '<value>')" when the length is wrong, and "<name> must be hexadecimal string (not '<value>')" when the length is right but the characters are not hex -- both at +rpc-invalid-parameter+ (-8). Keep %wallet-parse-txid as a one-line wrapper passing "txid" so its other caller (src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2925) is unaffected, and pass "blockhash" at src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1996. A regression test should assert the three strings wallet_listsinceblock.py and wallet_basic.py assert verbatim, since a test that only checks the -8 code would stay green through this whole divergence.
